{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent primary endpoint definition between synopsis and body",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving an IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1 at week 16",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Synopsis Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis defines the primary endpoint as IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1, but the body text (Section 4.1) may use a different definition (e.g., with or without improvement of at least 2 points). This discrepancy could lead to misalignment in analysis and interpretation.",
      "fix": "Ensure the primary endpoint definition is identical in the synopsis and the body, including any required improvement from baseline."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing trial schema (M11 1.2)",
      "quote": "Study Design This is a global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study",
      "page": 25,
      "section": "M11 1.2 Trial Schema",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol lacks a trial schema figure, which is required by ICH M11 to visually summarize the study design, including screening, treatment, and follow-up periods.",
      "fix": "Add a trial schema figure showing the study periods, visits, and key assessments."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent sample size and power calculation",
      "quote": "This sample size will yield >85% power to detect a treatment difference of 24% in the proportion of patients achieving IGA hand and foot (0, 1) at week 16 between placebo (10%) and dupilumab (34%)",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "Statistical Plan",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The power calculation uses a 24% difference (10% vs 34%), but the text later mentions an observed effect of 26% from prior studies, which is inconsistent. Also, the sample size of 130 with 10% dropout may not yield >85% power if the true difference is 24%.",
      "fix": "Clarify the assumed event rates and effect size, and recalculate the sample size to ensure consistency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing contraception requirements (M11 5.4)",
      "quote": "Laboratory testing will include ... pregnancy testing",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "M11 5.4 Contraception",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions pregnancy testing but does not specify contraception requirements for participants of reproductive potential, which is a critical safety and regulatory requirement.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed contraception section specifying acceptable methods, duration, and responsibilities for both male and female participants."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing trial stopping rules (M11 4.3)",
      "quote": "The end of study is defined as the date of the last visit of the last patient in the study.",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "M11 4.3 Trial Stopping Rules",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe any stopping rules for the trial, such as futility, safety, or administrative reasons, which are required by ICH M11.",
      "fix": "Add a section on trial stopping rules, including criteria for early termination and the process for decision-making."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent dosing for adolescents",
      "quote": "In adolescents: Body weight ≥60 kg, dupilumab 300 mg, after a loading dose of 600 mg on day 1, body weight <60 kg, dupilumab 200 mg, after a loading dose of 400 mg on day 1",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "Treatments",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis provides weight-based dosing for adolescents, but the body text (Section 6.1) may not specify the same, leading to potential dosing errors.",
      "fix": "Ensure the body text includes the same weight-based dosing regimen for adolescents as in the synopsis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing access to trial intervention after end of trial (M11 4.5)",
      "quote": "Post-treatment follow-up period: Upon completing the 16-weeks randomized treatment period, patients will enter a 12-week follow-up period.",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "M11 4.5 Access to Trial Intervention After End of Trial",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe whether patients will have access to dupilumab after the end of the trial, which is an ethical and regulatory requirement.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing post-trial access to the investigational product or alternative treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing data sharing and patient/public involvement (SPIRIT 6, 11)",
      "quote": "Statistical Plan The planned sample size is approximately 130 patients",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "SPIRIT 6, 11",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol lacks sections on data sharing and patient/public involvement, which are required by SPIRIT 2025.",
      "fix": "Add sections describing plans for data sharing and how patients/public were involved in the trial design or conduct."
    }
  ]
}
